facebook.long_form:
TODAY IS THE DAY — STEPH CURRY'S EXTENSION WINDOW IS OPEN

August 29, 2026, is a date Warriors fans have been circling for months — and now it's here.

Today marks the first day Stephen Curry is eligible to sign a contract extension with Golden State, and based on every available signal, the deal should come together quickly. The framework on the table: a two-year max extension worth $136.7 million, which would carry the four-time champion through the 2028-29 season and his age-40 campaign.

General manager Mike Dunleavy has made no secret of where this is headed. He's publicly stated his confidence that Curry will finish his career as a Warrior — multiple times, to multiple reporters. ESPN's Anthony Slater reported that both sides are "engaged with a mutual desire" to get the deal done.

The stakes are real. If Curry doesn't sign by the deadline, he becomes an unrestricted free agent after 2026-27 — the first time in 18 years that he'd ever hit the open market. Nobody is letting that happen.

Golden State went 37-45 last season. Keeping Curry isn't just about sentiment — it's the foundation everything else gets built on. Today is Day 1 of making that official.

What does the Chef do with the extension? Drop a 🏀 below!

facebook.long_form:
SHAEDON SHARPE SURGERY UPDATE — BLAZERS FACE LONG WAIT

Portland Trail Blazers fans received the news they feared: Shaedon Sharpe underwent surgery to repair a lateral meniscus tear in his right knee, and he won't be evaluated for return until late February 2027 at the earliest.

The surgery was performed by Dr. Kristofer Jones at the UCLA Department of Orthopedic Surgery and Sports Medicine. The Blazers confirmed a six-month reevaluation window — an important distinction, because that is NOT a guaranteed return date. Meniscus repairs vary widely in recovery. February is a checkpoint, not a finish line.

Sharpe's absence is a massive loss. He averaged 20.8 points, 4.3 rebounds, and 2.6 assists in 50 games last season — a breakout campaign that had the basketball world buzzing about his ceiling. Portland brought in Ja Morant this offseason to pair with Sharpe in what was supposed to be one of the league's most dangerous young backcourts.

That plan is shelved before it even starts. Morant opens training camp as Portland's only established star. The pressure on him is enormous.

Drop a 💙 for Shaedon's speedy recovery 🙏

facebook.long_form:
THE KAWHI LEONARD SAGA IS OVER — HE'S GOING BACK TO TORONTO

After two months of waiting, the longest offseason saga in the NBA is finally reaching its conclusion.

The NBA cleared the Los Angeles Clippers of cap circumvention in their investigation into payments made to Kawhi Leonard through the now-bankrupt company Aspiration. With that investigation resolved, the blockbuster trade sending Leonard back to Toronto can now be officially finalized.

The deal: Leonard to the Raptors in exchange for Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick, two unprotected first-round picks (2031 and 2033), one pick swap, and two second-round picks. Agreed in principle June 30, put on hold July 9, now cleared to complete.

Leonard was cleared personally throughout this process — the liability belonged to the Clippers organization. Toronto's training camp opens September 28 in Quebec City.

Seven years after Kawhi's iconic corner four bounced on the rim and fell through to send Toronto to the 2019 Finals — where he won championship and Finals MVP — he is coming home.

Drop a 🦖 if you're hyped!

facebook.long_form:
CAPTAIN WEMBANYAMA IS MAKING THE WORLD WATCH

Victor Wembanyama isn't just dominating the NBA — he's leading his country to what looks like an inevitable World Cup qualification.

France improved to 6-1 in Group L of the FIBA Basketball World Cup 2027 European Qualifiers, with Wembanyama recording 22 points and nine rebounds while shooting 60 percent from the field in their most recent qualifying win over Slovenia.

Wembanyama was named captain of the French national team for this qualifying window, taking over the armband from Rudy Gobert. He has embraced that role fully — leading France on both ends of the floor with a level of dominance that no European qualifying opponent has been able to match.

France faces Sweden on August 30 — their final game in this qualifying window. A win would push France closer to punching their ticket to the 2027 World Cup. The competition isn't there yet. France is.

After this, the focus shifts entirely to San Antonio. And if these qualifiers are any indication, Wemby's 2026-27 season is going to be something special.

Who's watching France vs. Sweden tomorrow? 👇

facebook.long_form:
NBA OPENING NIGHT IS GOING TO BE UNFORGETTABLE — OCTOBER 20, 2026

October 20. Write it down. The NBA's new season opens with the most compelling slate of Opening Night games in recent memory — three matchups on NBC, and every single one carries massive storylines.

The centerpiece: Philadelphia 76ers vs. New York Knicks at 7 PM ET at Madison Square Garden. The Knicks raise their first championship banner since 1973. And walking in as the villain? LeBron James and Jaylen Brown, making their 76ers debuts at one of basketball's loudest arenas on the most charged night of the year.

The night opens at 3 PM ET with Boston at Detroit, and closes at 9:30 PM ET with Oklahoma City hosting San Antonio — a rematch of last season's Western Conference Finals.

All three games on NBC and Peacock. First time EVER a broadcast network airs three NBA Tip-Off games. The league-NBC partnership is hitting a new gear.

October 20. Are you ready? 🏀

[Window: 7:00 PM ET]
